general.colorThemeHint: Works with both light and dark mode.
general.animatedBackgroundHint: Adds a living scene (e.g. the Full Moon 🌕 night sky) for scenic themes. Automatically paused under reduced-motion.

mascot.title: DY Mascot
mascot.enabledHint: Enabled by default. When off, the floating mascot is hidden app-wide.
mascot.modeHint: Inside app keeps the fox within the Devdy window. Desktop pet floats it in a frameless, always-on-top window over your desktop.
mascot.soundHint: Let the fox speak the bubble text aloud with your system's text-to-speech when it has something to say.
mascot.agentSpeechHint: When enabled, important moments can wait for a lightweight AI call so the mascot comments on the actual session result. Off by default.
mascot.voiceHint: The fox speaks the bubble text with the system voice matching the app language. Install more voices in macOS System Settings → Accessibility → Spoken Content → Manage Voices.
mascot.liteHint: Trims the heaviest visual effects (glow tails, orbit blur, ground-dot density) for weaker machines. All motion stays; effects look slightly simpler. "Auto" enables lite mode when a weak machine is detected (few CPU cores or low RAM).
mascot.previewHint: Pick a state to preview its animation, sound and speech bubble together.
mascot.testBubbleSample: Heads up — this is a sample notification.

levels.currentHint: The fox levels up on its own as you spend tokens — no manual setup. After the peak realm it reincarnates and earns a star ⭐, so levels never cap out.
levels.previewHint: Pick a realm and tier to preview how the level will appear in the mascot preview.

changes.tier1: Freshly entered realm: the aura shifts lightly while breathing and eyes feel steadier.
changes.tier2: Energy becomes clearer: brighter eyes and a stronger ground ring.
changes.tier3: Spiritual energy gathers: small spark beats appear while AI is thinking or running tools.
changes.tier4: Near completion: tails and energy streams become stronger during loading.
changes.tier5: Realm complete: the badge becomes more prominent and is ready for the next breakthrough effect.

mcp.title: Built-in MCP Server
mcp.devdyHint: Injects a built-in devdy MCP server into every run so the AI can use your own data while chatting — quick notes, cross-session recall, project context (file tree & git) and managed VPS. Tools appear as mcp__devdy__*; write & remote actions still go through the permission prompt. Takes effect on the next run.

google.title: Google Account (Drive + Gmail)
google.intro: Connect one or more Google accounts so the AI can work with your Drive files and Gmail. Tools appear as mcp__gdrive__* and mcp__gmail__*; with multiple accounts the AI targets one via each tool's account argument (the default account when omitted). Write, delete, share and send actions still go through the permission prompt. Refresh tokens are stored in your OS Keychain (never written to disk). Takes effect on the next run.
google.credsWarning: Create your own OAuth Desktop app credentials in Google Cloud Console, enable the Drive API and Gmail API, then paste the Client ID and Secret below.
google.credsSaved: OAuth credentials saved — no need to re-enter them.
google.enterLabel: Enter a label for the account (e.g. work, personal).
google.enterBothCreds: Enter both Client ID and Client Secret.
google.removeMessage: The AI will lose access to this account. Your saved OAuth credentials are kept so you can re-add it without re-entering them.
google.forgetMessage: This removes the stored Client ID/Secret and ALL connected accounts. You will need to paste the credentials again next time.

github.title: GitHub Accounts
github.intro: Add GitHub accounts once and link them to projects. PATs are stored securely in your OS Keychain (never written to disk). Required scopes: repo (private) or public_repo (public).
github.isolationWarning: Keep this machine logged out of gh globally: do not run gh auth login or set GH_TOKEN system-wide. Devdy wires the correct per-project credential at run time; a global login would let runs bypass that isolation.
github.patPlaceholder: New PAT (leave blank to keep current)
github.deleteMessage: Delete this GitHub account? Projects linked to it will be unlinked.

gitlab.title: GitLab Accounts
gitlab.intro: Add GitLab accounts once and link them to projects. PATs are stored securely in your OS Keychain (never written to disk). Set a custom host for self-hosted GitLab, and an optional commit email. Required scope: api (or read_api + write_repository) — a repository-only token is rejected by the validation endpoint.
gitlab.isolationWarning: Keep this machine logged out of glab globally: do not run glab auth login or set GITLAB_TOKEN system-wide. Devdy wires the correct per-project credential at run time; a global login would let runs bypass that isolation.
gitlab.patPlaceholder: New PAT (leave blank to keep current)
gitlab.deleteMessage: Delete this GitLab account? Projects linked to it will be unlinked.

aws.title: AWS Accounts
aws.intro: Add AWS accounts once and link one account to each project. Secret Access Keys and Session Tokens are stored securely in your OS Keychain. Devdy wires the selected project account to Claude and Codex runs through the broker.
aws.isolationWarning: Avoid setting AWS credentials globally for agent work. Devdy gates aws calls through its broker; credential/config mutation such as aws configure is blocked.
aws.newSecretPlaceholder: New Secret Access Key (leave blank to keep current)
aws.sessionTokenReplacePlaceholder: Session Token (optional; set when replacing secret)
aws.deleteMessage: Delete this AWS account? Projects linked to it will be unlinked.

ai.title: AI & Models
ai.reloadModelsTitle: Reload the model list from your Claude account
ai.modelsLoadError: Could not load dynamic models — using the default list.
ai.codexStaticHint: Codex does not support dynamic model listing — this list is fixed.
ai.permissionHint: How tool calls are gated (Claude & Codex). "Ask via UI" surfaces each request in a modal; "Bypass all" skips the modal — fast, but unsafe outside trusted directories. You can still override engine, model and permission mode per run on the Run screen.
ai.translationHint: Used for translating highlighted text in the Run AI screen.
ai.translateModelHint: "Default" → picks a fast model (Claude uses Haiku) for faster translation.

usage.title: Usage & Budget
usage.contextMeterHint: Shows how full the current run's context window is. The bar turns amber past the warn threshold and offers a one-click /compact.
usage.limitOverrideHint: Leave the override empty to auto-resolve from the model (Claude 200k / 1M, Codex 272k).
usage.budgetHint: Checked before each run & follow-up: Devdy blocks a new run (override per turn) when the run's engine reaches a limit below. Thresholds map to that engine's real subscription plan windows (from /usage) — a rolling 5h window and a weekly window (resets per account). A run is blocked if any set window is reached. Codex usually exposes only the weekly window, so set Weekly to cover it. Leave a field empty to skip that window; with no plan data (e.g. API-key sessions) the guardrail is inactive.
